title: Quantification and Size-profiling of Extracellular Vesicles Using Tunable Resistive Pulse Sensing
protocol: Connect the instrument to a computer with Izon Control Suite software installed.
Choose the NP150 nanopore for EVs in the size range 85 - 300 nm.
Select NP200 nanopore for EVs in the size range 100 - 400 nm.
Use NP100 pore for EVs isolated using a protocol that removes larger EVs, targeting sizes 70 - 200 nm.
Choose NP200 nanopore when working with EVs in biological samples or different isolation protocols.
Select NP300 nanopore for EVs in the size range 150 - 600 nm.
Use NP400 nanopore for larger types of EVs, targeting sizes 200 - 800 nm.
Choose CPC100 polystyrene calibration particles for NP100 nanopores.
Select CP100 and CPC200 particles for NP150 and NP200 nanopores, respectively.
Vortex the calibration particles briefly (30 sec) to ensure homogeneity.
Optionally apply sonication to remove aggregates from calibration particles.
Dilute calibration particles in PBS to the target concentration in at least 40 µl volume.
Apply and remove 78 µl of PBS on the lower fluid cell.
Measure the distance between two opposite arms using digital calipers and enter into the “Stretch” input field, then click “calibrate stretch”.
Increase the distance between opposing arms to 47 mm by turning the side wheel.
Reapply 78 µl PBS to the lower fluid cell after stretching.
Ensure the laptop is connected to a grounded power grid when running Izon Control Suite software.
Keep mobile phones away from the instrument to avoid electrical interference.
Place the upper fluid cell and shielding cage on the nanopore.
Introduce 40 μl of diluted calibration particles into the upper fluid cell.
Apply ≥0.8 kPa positive pressure using the VPM.
Reduce the applied stretch slowly towards 44 mm whilst analyzing blockade events caused by calibration particles.
Reduce the stretch until appropriate blockade events are observed in the “Signal Trace” panel (mode >0.1 nA) and the corresponding particle rate is >100/min.
Place calibration particles in the upper fluid cell.
Apply pressure using the VPM and record >500 particles.
If performing a multi-pressure measurement, increase the applied pressure and record a second calibration file.
Remove the calibration sample from the upper fluid cell.
Wash the upper fluid cell 3 times with 100 μl PBS to remove residual particles.
Use lint-free tissue to remove any residual PBS from the upper fluid cell before introducing the sample.
Introduce the sample to the upper fluid cell.
Ensure the baseline current is within 3% of the observed baseline for calibration particles.
Apply pressures as applied during calibration particle measurement and record sample files.
If particle detection, baseline current, or RMS noise shows abnormal changes, pause recording.
To restore baseline, tap or twist the shielding cap, apply the plunger, or wash the nanopore with deionized water.
Alternatively, increase nanopore stretch to 47 mm with maximum pressure from VPM for approximately 5 min.
Click on the “Analyze Data” tab in the software.
Right-click the “Unprocessed Files” and select “Process Files” to process calibration and sample files.
Select corresponding sample and calibration files and click “OK” to couple them.
Centrifuge 100 µl of cell culture supernatant for 7 min at 300 x g.
Add 20 µl of the supernatant to 20 µl of PBS and 10 µl of 75 times diluted 335 nm polystyrene beads (stock 7e10/ml).
Measure the ‘calibration bead only’ sample first.
Ensure that the background detection of small non-bead particles is as low as possible (<10% of the beads).
Measure each individual sample once before recording replicates in order to distribute fluctuation in nanopore conditions equally over the different samples.
Measure at least 3 replicates of each sample.
Remeasure the ‘calibration bead only’ sample after finishing the recording of all samples.
Open the ‘calibration bead only’ sample and one or more sample files.
Determine the blockade event size (in nA) that distinguishes EVs from polystyrene beads.
Set equal bin sizes for all measurements in ‘ViewSettings’.
Retrieve total particle count for each sample using “Particle Analysis Summary” tab.
Filter data sets using the determined cut-off level via “Data Filtering” pop-up.
Display only particles smaller than the cut-off value.
Retrieve EV count from the “Particle Analysis Summary” tab for each sample.
Subtract EV count from total particle count to determine calibration bead amount.
Determine EV-to-bead ratio by dividing EV count by calibration bead count.
Average ratios determined for each “bead only” calibration sample to get background ratio.
Subtract average background ratio from each individual sample’s ratio.
Multiply adjusted EV-to-bead ratio by the concentration of calibration beads to determine EV concentration.
Multiply the concentration found by the dilution factor introduced by the addition of calibration beads.
Calculate statistics such as averages, standard deviation, and standard error of the mean for each group of replicates.
Determine a “bead-to-EV” ratio using samples without spiked polystyrene beads if correction for underestimation is required.
Add the bead-to-EV ratio to the EV-to-bead ratio determined in step 2.3.8.
Open a sample recording twice in the Control Suite Software.
Set filter options of one sample to display particles bigger than the cut-off determined above.
This will display the calibration particles only.
Set the filtered sample to “calibration file” and enter the mode size of the calibration beads.
Couple the sample file and the “calibration file” created in step 2.4.3 as described in 1.4.2.
Display the size distribution of both EVs and calibration beads based on the spiked calibration beads.
Use an EV sample spiked with calibration particles for EV size-estimation when exact buffer components are unknown.
